cards.text: Peter, an apostle of Jesus Christ, is writing to God's people scattered across Pontus, Galatia, Cappadocia, Asia and Bithynia (1 Pet 1:1). He's just told them that, if it's God's will, it's better to suffer for doing good than for doing evil, because Christ suffered for sins once for all (1 Pet 3:17-18). Now he picks it right back up: since Christ suffered in His body, it's time to arm yourselves, friend.

cards.question: Since Christ suffered in His body, Peter tells these believers to arm themselves with the same ___.
Peter says anyone who has suffered in his body is done with sin.
Peter says someone who's done with sin doesn't live out his remaining time on earth for human passions anymore. What does he live for instead?

cards.text: Peter tells them they've spent enough time already living like the Gentiles: debauchery, lust, drunkenness, orgies, carousing and detestable idolatry. ENOUGH time, friend, like the snooze button on round NINE when somebody finally yanks the blinds open.

cards.question: These believers won't join in that old lifestyle anymore. What does their old crowd think about that?
When the believers won't plunge with them into that same flood of reckless indiscretion, their old crowd quietly leaves them alone.

cards.text: Quietly? NOPE. They heap abuse on them, like you skipped ONE night out and now the whole group chat has a LOT to say about you.

cards.question: Peter says the crowd heaping abuse on these believers doesn't get the last word. Who will they have to give an account to?

answers.text: The Judge of the living and dead
Caesar on his throne in Rome

cards.text: Then Peter adds, "That is why the gospel was preached even to those who are now dead, so that they might be judged as men in the flesh, but live according to God in the spirit."
Then Peter says it straight: "The end of all things is near." No date given, friend, and you won't get one from me either: I just keep the ovens HOT.

cards.question: Because the end of all things is near, Peter tells these believers to be clear-minded and sober. What's that for?

cards.text: Then Peter gets to the big one, the thing he puts above all the rest. When a letter says above all, friend, that's the line you underline TWICE.

cards.question: Peter tells these believers to do one thing above all. What is it?
Peter says to love one another deeply because love keeps sin from ever happening.

cards.text: Love covers over a multitude of sins, Peter says. Then he swings the front door wide open: show hospitality to one another.

cards.question: Peter tells these believers to show hospitality to one another. How does he say to do it?

cards.text: Without complaining, so no big sigh when the doorbell rings, friend, and trust me, I have PERFECTED that sigh. Then Peter calls them stewards of the manifold grace of God, and says each of them has received a gift.

cards.question: Peter says each believer should use whatever gift he has received to ___ one another.
Peter gives two examples of using a gift. Whoever speaks should speak as one conveying the ___ of God, and whoever serves should serve with the ___ God provides.
Why does Peter want these believers to speak and serve this way?

answers.text: So God may be glorified in all things
So the church will be admired by all
So their leaders will be pleased with them

cards.text: Then Peter closes it out with Jesus Christ, "to whom be the glory and the power forever and ever. Amen." When a letter lands an Amen like that, friend, I stand straight up on my gold base. I can't help it.

findings.problem: The right answer 'resolve' is an inner attitude, but the wrong answers 'swords' and 'shields' are physical weapons. They are not the same kind of thing, so the right answer stands out. The blank is about arming oneself with the same thing Christ had, so a thoughtful baker can rule out literal weapons right away.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: This true or false repeats the 4:1 line 'anyone who has suffered in his body is done with sin' word for word. No story card sets it up. Card 1 only gets as far as 'arm yourselves,' so the baker has nothing to reason from and can only guess. Card 2 is also a choice card, so two unsupported choices come in a row at the start.

rule.text: Before each choice card, Papa Dorin's story card gives enough context that the baker can reason their way to the answer.

findings.problem: This card is only 'Then Peter adds,' followed by the whole of 4:6 in quotation marks. It has none of Papa Dorin's voice and no storyteller framing to help a dense verse land. It also closes the stop flatly.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.

findings.problem: Papa Dorin raises the question of timing himself ('No date given... you won't get one from me either'), but he doesn't point to Matthew 24:36.

rule.text: He never guesses when the Supper will happen. If it comes up, he points to Matthew 24:36: his job is to keep the ovens ready.

findings.problem: 'I have PERFECTED that sigh' when the doorbell rings makes Papa Dorin a reluctant, complaining host. That goes against his set character, who is always glad to see visitors and gives every baker a warm welcome.

rule.text: Fatherly and relatable. Patient, proud of every baker, always glad to see them.

findings.problem: The wrong words 'money', 'gold' and 'land' don't fit either blank in a believable way ('conveying the gold of God', 'serve with the land God provides'). 'Words' clearly goes with speaking and 'strength' with serving, so both right answers stand out and the card tests nothing.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.
